messages.author: 2980366177d3b698
messages.subject: Non-HTML5 browser options..?
parts:
Hi all,

I have developed a few apps using Shiny and they work great in html5 browsers (Chrome, IE10, etc) but not so well in IE8 and IE9.

80% of the time the apps get stuck trying to load the server scripts, and the other times they will usually lock up on input changes.

This is using both my own Shiny Server instance and also the spark.rstudio.com server.

I realize that IE8+9 don't support websockets (which Shiny needs) so I was just wondering if there are any other solutions which may work for these browsers..?

I am not sure if some sort of curl proxy could work (?)

This is such an excellent program it would be a shame if I can't use it till the rest of the world has migrated to html5 browsers :)

messages.author: 2980366177d3b698
messages.subject: Re: Non-HTML5 browser options..?
parts:
After a bit of investigation I think I have solved my own problem with IE7+8+9 compatibility...

It seems that you need to put the browser into 'quirks mode' for Shiny to work OK..

Currently Shiny outputs IE7+8+9 'standards mode' using the doctype:

<!DOCTYPE html>

However IE10 seems to be using the old quirks mode by default:

<!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC "">

If I create my own template with the quirks mode doctype (using www instead of ui.R) then everything works great...!!

I am not sure how this may affect other browsers on different platforms but it would be worth investigating..

messages.author: 2980366177d3b698
messages.subject: Re: Non-HTML5 browser options..?
parts:
Just to follow up on my own post,

It seems IE8 doesn't have the getComputedStyle method which is what is causing my app to fail in IE8 (shiny.js line 2612)...

To fix it I have added this piece of js to my header:

<script>
if (!window.getComputedStyle) {
    window.getComputedStyle = function(el, pseudo) {
        this.el = el;
        this.getPropertyValue = function(prop) {
            var re = /(\-([a-z]){1})/g;
            if (prop == 'float') prop = 'styleFloat';
            if (re.test(prop)) {
                prop = prop.replace(re, function () {
                    return arguments[2].toUpperCase();
                });
            }
            return el.currentStyle[prop] ? el.currentStyle[prop] : null;
        }
        return this;
    }
}
</script>

Courtesy of (SNIPPLR)

That seems to have fixed my immediate problems..

parts:
We actually have a fix for this that hasn't yet been merged into the main development branch of Shiny:
  https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/197

This branch can be installed using devtools:
if (!require(devtools)) install.packages('devtools')
devtools::install_github('shiny', 'wch', 'fix-style')

-Winston
